endpointResults.population: 13 children with severe AADC deficiency, aged approximately 16 months to 10 years and with adequate skull maturity; no gross motor milestones at baseline. Twelve were assessed at week 48.

Clinical function, circulating NfL and cell distribution/target engagement are separate observations; none demonstrates that the mapped cell subtype mediated this clinical trend.

cellObservations.comparator: Untreated Npc1−/− littermates

cellObservations.population: Female BALB/c Npc1−/− mice; five animals per acetyl-leucine treatment group; pre-symptomatic dietary dosing from age 3 weeks, assessment at day 59. Different drug formulation from marketed Aqneursa.

cellObservations.claim: Racemic DL treatment increased Purkinje-cell counts versus untreated mutants in lobules I–II (+133%, p=0.0027) and III (+402%, p=0.0108). The published purified-L arm did not reproduce significant preservation; DL results cannot be credited to Aqneursa.
cellObservations.studyRelationship: Different preclinical system and different formulation from the clinical trial; included to prevent incorrect formulation transfer.
cellObservations.comparator: Untreated Npc1−/− littermates

cellObservations.population: NPC1-deficient Chinese hamster ovary cell model; an in-vitro system, not treated human neurons
cellObservations.species: Chinese hamster ovary cells in vitro

cellObservations.assay: LysoTracker-based relative acidic-compartment volume by live-cell flow cytometry
cellObservations.timeFrame: 24 and 72 hours

cellObservations.comparator: Untreated NPC1-deficient cells; wild-type cells as reference

limitations: Diagnosis crosswalks are discovery links. They do not assert that a displayed ClinVar allele was enrolled, responsive or treatment-eligible.

diseaseIds.label: Achondroplasia
diseaseIds.rationale: Reviewed condition identity; discovery crosswalk only, not evidence that every disease-associated allele was enrolled or responsive.

endpointResults.label: Short stature
endpointResults.population: 84 randomized children with genetically confirmed achondroplasia, eligible age 2–11; 57 navepegritide 100 micrograms CNP/kg/week and 27 placebo.
endpointResults.comparator: Randomized placebo, double blind
endpointResults.analysis: ANCOVA; full randomized analysis with multiple imputation for missing height. Growth rate is an intermediate endpoint.
endpointResults.summary: LS mean AGV 5.89 vs 4.41 cm/year; difference +1.49 (95% CI 1.05–1.93), P<0.001. FDA accelerated approval uses AGV to predict final adult height.
limits: Positive growth-rate result does not establish final adult height, normalization of stature or prevention of neurological complications.

endpointResults.label: Short stature
endpointResults.population: 84 randomized children with genetically confirmed achondroplasia, eligible age 2–11; 57 navepegritide 100 micrograms CNP/kg/week and 27 placebo.
endpointResults.comparator: Randomized placebo
endpointResults.analysis: ANCOVA, prespecified multiple-testing strategy; untreated-achondroplasia reference distribution.
endpointResults.summary: LS difference +0.28 Z-score units (95% CI 0.18–0.39); height improved relative to the achondroplasia reference distribution.
limits: This reference is other children with achondroplasia, not normal-population adult height.

endpointResults.label: Short stature
endpointResults.population: 84 randomized children with genetically confirmed achondroplasia, eligible age 2–11; 57 navepegritide 100 micrograms CNP/kg/week and 27 placebo.
endpointResults.comparator: Randomized placebo
endpointResults.analysis: FDA review ANCOVA; not included in the confirmatory multiple-testing strategy despite listed registry-secondary status.
endpointResults.summary: LS difference +0.30 Z-score units (95% CI 0.16–0.45); nominal analysis.
limits: Exploratory result; final adult height and complete correction of short stature remain unconfirmed.

endpointResults.label: Disproportionate short stature
endpointResults.endpoint: Change in upper-to-lower body segment ratio
endpointResults.population: 84 randomized children with genetically confirmed achondroplasia, eligible age 2–11; 57 navepegritide 100 micrograms CNP/kg/week and 27 placebo.
endpointResults.comparator: Randomized placebo
endpointResults.analysis: Exploratory ANCOVA comparison of body proportions, distinct from growth velocity.
endpointResults.summary: LS difference −0.02 (95% CI −0.07–0.03); the randomized ratio comparison did not establish proportionality improvement.
limits: A ratio is one aspect of disproportionate short stature; increased growth alone is not proportionality rescue.

endpointResults.label: Genu varum
endpointResults.population: 84 randomized children with genetically confirmed achondroplasia, eligible age 2–11; 57 navepegritide 100 micrograms CNP/kg/week and 27 placebo.
endpointResults.comparator: Randomized placebo
endpointResults.analysis: Exploratory LS mean comparison; no multiple-testing-adjusted inference. Most baseline angles indicated varus.
endpointResults.summary: LS difference −1.81 degrees (95% CI −3.16 to −0.47), favoring the drug on this leg-alignment measure.
limits: Angle change does not establish elimination of genu varum or avoidance of corrective surgery.

endpointResults.label: Short stature
endpointResults.endpoint: Annualized growth velocity in dose-finding trial
endpointResults.population: 57 prepubertal children age 2–10 with genetic confirmation; 11 received 100 micrograms/kg/week, 15 pooled placebo; other active cohorts received lower doses.
endpointResults.comparator: Pooled randomized placebo across dose cohorts
endpointResults.analysis: Full-analysis-set ANCOVA of dose cohort against pooled placebo.
endpointResults.summary: At 100 micrograms/kg/week AGV was 5.42 vs 4.35 cm/year, P=0.0218; supports the dose chosen for APPROACH.
limits: Small dose-specific cohort; other doses and longer open-label periods cannot be pooled as a new randomized comparison.

endpointResults.comparator: Randomized placebo
endpointResults.label: Achondroplasia Child Experience Measure: Physical Functioning
endpointResults.endpoint: Change in caregiver-reported ACEM Physical Functioning score
endpointResults.population: Full randomized cohort: 57 navepegritide and 27 placebo; observed week-52 scores in 54 and 26 respectively. FDA multiple-imputation analysis retains full denominators.
endpointResults.analysis: ANCOVA with treatment, stratification factor, baseline age and baseline score; prespecified key secondary included in graphical multiple-testing strategy. Missing scores multiply imputed. FDA reports nominal P=0.22; no multiplicity-controlled significance.
endpointResults.summary: LS change 0.4 versus 5.3 points; difference −4.9 (95% CI −12.6 to 2.9), P=0.22. Higher scores mean greater impairment.
limits: No sufficiently specific HPO mapping asserted for this broad caregiver scale.
Overall physical-function benefit was not established; favorable younger-child/subgroup results cannot replace the full-cohort result.
FDA stated ACEM/SF-10 measures had not been shown fit for purpose in this programme.

endpointResults.comparator: Randomized placebo
endpointResults.label: SF-10 Physical Health Summary
endpointResults.endpoint: Change in caregiver-reported Short Form 10 Physical Health Summary score
endpointResults.population: APPROACH age ≥5 years at baseline: 36 navepegritide and 17 placebo; observed week-52 scores in 32 and 16. Multiple-imputation analysis retains 36/17.
endpointResults.analysis: ANCOVA with treatment, stratification factor, baseline age and baseline SF-10 score; prespecified age-eligible subset included in graphical multiple-testing strategy. Missing scores multiply imputed. FDA reports nominal P=0.64; no multiplicity-controlled significance.
endpointResults.summary: LS change −6.3 versus −4.5 points; difference −1.8 (95% CI −9.3 to 5.7), P=0.64. The scale is a broad physical-health summary.
limits: No gait, joint-mobility or other specific HPO phenotype inferred from this broad scale.
Subset excludes children below five; observed-score denominators differ from imputed analysis denominators.
FDA did not accept these patient-reported measures as demonstrated fit for purpose in this programme.

cellObservations.population: Neonatal Fgfr3Y367C/+ achondroplasia-like model; no human trial patients.

cellObservations.comparator: Nonclinical model comparison; accessible review does not report a complete group-level sample size.

cellObservations.assay: Plasma cGMP quantitative radioimmunoassay
cellObservations.timeFrame: Clinical programme through 52 weeks

cellObservations.studyRelationship: Samples in the outcome-study programme, but no participant-level growth-plate mediation test; dose was not selected using cGMP.
cellObservations.comparator: Dose/exposure comparison; no cell-isolated comparator.

cellObservations.population: Healthy juvenile male cynomolgus monkeys without FGFR3 overactivation.

cellObservations.comparator: Vosoritide positive control; healthy animals rather than mutant-achondroplasia controls.

endpointResults.label: Ectopic ossification
endpointResults.endpoint: Number of new CT-detected heterotopic ossification lesions, 10 mg/kg
endpointResults.population: 63 adults with genetically confirmed FOP and CAJIS ≤19; 95% ACVR1 R206H. Randomized 23 to 10 mg/kg, 19 to 3 mg/kg and 21 to placebo, IV every four weeks.
endpointResults.comparator: Randomized placebo, 21 patients
endpointResults.analysis: Negative-binomial regression; multiplicity controlled across the two primary dose comparisons.
endpointResults.summary: Two new lesions in 23 high-dose patients versus 19 in 21 placebo patients; rate ratio 0.10 (95% CI 0.01–0.76), P=0.026.

endpointResults.label: Ectopic ossification

endpointResults.population: 63 adults with genetically confirmed FOP and CAJIS ≤19; 95% ACVR1 R206H. Randomized 23 to 10 mg/kg, 19 to 3 mg/kg and 21 to placebo, IV every four weeks.
endpointResults.comparator: Randomized placebo, 21 patients
endpointResults.analysis: Negative-binomial regression; multiplicity controlled for the primary dose comparisons.
endpointResults.summary: One new lesion in 19 low-dose patients versus 19 in 21 placebo patients; rate ratio 0.06 (95% CI 0.00–0.73), P=0.027.
limits: Rounded lower CI is not a proven zero risk; 3 mg/kg is distinct from the labeled starting dose.

endpointResults.label: Ectopic ossification
endpointResults.endpoint: Proportion of patients developing new HO lesions
endpointResults.population: 63 adults with genetically confirmed FOP and CAJIS ≤19; 95% ACVR1 R206H. Randomized 23 to 10 mg/kg, 19 to 3 mg/kg and 21 to placebo, IV every four weeks.
endpointResults.comparator: Randomized placebo
endpointResults.analysis: Barnard unconditional exact test; secondary hierarchy stopped at this endpoint for 10 mg/kg and earlier for 3 mg/kg.
endpointResults.summary: New-lesion patients: 2/23 at 10 mg/kg, 1/19 at 3 mg/kg and 5/21 placebo; nominal P=0.22 and 0.12 respectively.
limits: Nonsignificance does not establish equal incidence; this is a different estimand from the successful lesion-count primary.

endpointResults.label: Ectopic ossification
endpointResults.endpoint: Total volume of new HO lesions
endpointResults.population: 63 adults with genetically confirmed FOP and CAJIS ≤19; 95% ACVR1 R206H. Randomized 23 to 10 mg/kg, 19 to 3 mg/kg and 21 to placebo, IV every four weeks.
endpointResults.comparator: Randomized placebo
endpointResults.analysis: Prespecified Wilcoxon rank-sum test; nominal after secondary hierarchy failure. Mean-difference bootstrap CIs use a different statistic.
endpointResults.summary: Mean new-HO volume 0.02 cm³ at 10 mg/kg, 0.01 at 3 mg/kg and 10.45 placebo; nominal rank-test P=0.13 and 0.085.
limits: Bootstrap mean-difference CIs excluding zero do not override the nonsignificant prespecified rank tests.

endpointResults.label: Pain
endpointResults.endpoint: Number of clinician-assessed FOP flare-ups, 10 mg/kg
endpointResults.population: 63 adults with genetically confirmed FOP and CAJIS ≤19; 95% ACVR1 R206H. Randomized 23 to 10 mg/kg, 19 to 3 mg/kg and 21 to placebo, IV every four weeks.
endpointResults.comparator: Randomized placebo
endpointResults.analysis: Negative-binomial regression, exposure-duration offset; first key-secondary test passed for 10 mg/kg.
endpointResults.summary: Nine clinician-assessed flares at 10 mg/kg versus 66 placebo; rate ratio 0.12 (95% CI 0.03–0.42), P=0.001.
limits: Flare-ups combine painful swelling and other features; this does not isolate pain intensity or restore joint function.

endpointResults.label: Pain
endpointResults.endpoint: Number of clinician-assessed FOP flare-ups, 3 mg/kg
endpointResults.population: 63 adults with genetically confirmed FOP and CAJIS ≤19; 95% ACVR1 R206H. Randomized 23 to 10 mg/kg, 19 to 3 mg/kg and 21 to placebo, IV every four weeks.
endpointResults.comparator: Randomized placebo
endpointResults.analysis: First secondary hierarchy test for 3 mg/kg.
endpointResults.summary: 53 flares at 3 mg/kg versus 66 placebo; rate ratio 0.85 (95% CI 0.26–2.73), P=0.78.
limits: Do not transfer the high-dose flare result to the lower dose.

endpointResults.label: Pain
endpointResults.endpoint: Patients reporting FOP flare-ups in daily diary
endpointResults.population: 63 adults with genetically confirmed FOP and CAJIS ≤19; 95% ACVR1 R206H. Randomized 23 to 10 mg/kg, 19 to 3 mg/kg and 21 to placebo, IV every four weeks.
endpointResults.comparator: Randomized placebo
endpointResults.analysis: Barnard exact test; nominal comparisons after hierarchy stopped.
endpointResults.summary: 11/23 at 10 mg/kg and 11/19 at 3 mg/kg reported flare-ups versus 13/21 placebo; nominal P=0.53 and 0.86.
limits: Diary and clinician assessments differ; clinical flare benefit is not uniform across methods.

endpointResults.label: Ectopic ossification

endpointResults.summary: LS treatment difference −24.6% (95% CI −51.8–2.5), P=0.0741; primary endpoint was not met.
limits: Post-hoc new-lesion results do not turn this primary analysis positive; established lesions did not show the anticipated response.

endpointResults.label: Pain
endpointResults.endpoint: Time-weighted change in daily average FOP pain numerical rating
endpointResults.population: Same 44-person LUMINA-1 randomized AHO population.
endpointResults.comparator: Randomized placebo

endpointResults.summary: LS difference −0.34 on the pain rating (95% CI −0.96–0.27); no established randomized pain improvement.
limits: Pain result is distinct from later OPTIMA clinician flare count; no confirmatory inference after hierarchy failure.

endpointResults.summary: New CT lesions occurred in 9/22 (40.9%) during placebo and 0/22 after crossover, P=0.0027; favorable observed change without randomized period-2 causality.
limits: Time, selection and open-label effects are not controlled; not independent randomized replication.
